tldr: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max launched Aug 3 claiming to beat GPT-5.6 Sol Max on agentic computer-use benchmarks; OpenAI answered three days later with a shipped Sol update rather than a rebuttal. An independent hands-on test on Aug 7 and a finance case study on Aug 10 each added real-world evidence for the updated model, still with no independent benchmark rebuttal to Qwen3.8-Max's claim.
whats_new: OpenAI answered Qwen3.8-Max a fourth time on Aug 13 with Ultrafast, a Cerebras-powered API tier running Sol up to 14X faster (750 tokens/sec) — another product ship, not a benchmark rebuttal.
why_it_matters: Ultrafast's Cerebras-backed 750-tok/sec tier is a real latency/throughput lever for agentic workloads, but it's a new pricing/availability decision layered on an already-unverified capability claim against Qwen3.8-Max.

status.state: Unverified vs. Qwen3.8-Max · speed tier added
status.detail: OpenAI keeps answering the Qwen3.8-Max claim with shipped product work — an accuracy update, a case study, now a speed-focused API tier — rather than an independent benchmark rebuttal.

beats.headline: Qwen3.8-Max claims to beat GPT-5.6 Sol Max on agentic computer use
beats.summary: Alibaba's model launch specifically targets Sol Max's agentic computer-use performance as the benchmark to beat.

beats.headline: OpenAI ships an improved Sol and widens free Luna access
beats.summary: OpenAI's own update post lands three days after the Qwen3.8-Max claim, improving Sol's accuracy and consistency in ChatGPT.

beats.headline: Independent test shows Sol Ultra building a full game end-to-end
beats.summary: Simon Willison's Codex + Sol Ultra build is the first outside look at the updated model's real-world output quality.

beats.headline: OpenAI publishes a finance case study: Sol turns research into traceable decks and workbooks
beats.summary: Model ML's story has Sol carrying finance research through to editable PowerPoint and Excel output, OpenAI's next answer to the Qwen3.8-Max challenge.

beats.headline: OpenAI previews Ultrafast: Sol at up to 14X speed on Cerebras hardware
beats.summary: A new API service tier delivers up to 750 output tokens/sec, OpenAI's fourth consecutive product answer instead of a benchmark rebuttal.

open_questions: Does an independent benchmark confirm Qwen3.8-Max's agentic computer-use win over Sol Max, or does the improved Sol close the gap?
What specifically changed in the 'improved' GPT-5.6 Sol — accuracy, latency, or tool-use reliability?
Does the Model ML case study's 'traceable' output claim hold up under third-party audit, or is it self-reported by OpenAI's customer story?
Are Ultrafast's 14X-speed and 750-tok/sec figures independently benchmarked, or are they OpenAI-reported like the other claims in this thread?
take_for_builders: If evaluating Sol for latency-sensitive agent workloads, test the new Ultrafast tier's throughput and pricing yourself — like the Qwen3.8-Max and Model ML claims, the 14X/750 tok/sec numbers are OpenAI-reported, not independently verified.
